subject: Re: Post-launch: pipeline attribution + tagging conventions (Benchmark Report)
body:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jul 22, 2025 at 9:14 AM PT
Subject: Post-launch: pipeline attribution + tagging conventions (Benchmark Report)

Team —

Now that the benchmark report is live and we’re getting inbound + outbound replies referencing it, we need a consistent way to measure (1) sourced pipeline and (2) influenced pipeline in HubSpot.

Below is a proposed attribution + tagging standard for the “Benchmark Report: Latency/$ (2025)” campaign. If we align on this today, Tyler and I can lock the dashboard + automate the weekly rollup.

---

1) WHAT WE’RE REPORTING

A) Sourced pipeline (strict)
- Deal create is attributable to benchmark campaign.
- Definition: Deal create date occurs within 7 days of first known benchmark touch AND that touch is the first touch in the buying journey (per HubSpot attribution).

B) Influenced pipeline (practical)
- Definition: Any deal where at least one associated contact has a benchmark touch within 90 days prior to deal create OR between deal create and first meeting held.
- We’ll report influenced as a separate number (NOT additive to sourced).

C) Activation / PLG assist (top-of-funnel)
- Benchmark landing page visits → signup → first key event (API key created / first successful call) tracked separately in Growth.

---

2) REQUIRED TAGS / FIELDS (HubSpot)

A) Campaign
- HubSpot campaign name (single source of truth):
  “Benchmark Report: Latency per Dollar — 2025 Launch”

B) UTMs for all benchmark links (email, social, partner, outbound, webinar follow-ups)
- utm_campaign=benchmark_report_2025
- utm_source = email | social | partner | outbound | community | webinar | press
- utm_medium = lifecycle | paid_social | organic_social | newsletter | sequence | referral
- utm_content = variant identifier (keep it short; see attached CSV)

C) Deal property (manual backstop when needed)
- Deal property: “Influenced campaigns (manual)” (multi-select)
  - Add option: “benchmark_report_2025”
- When to use it: only if the prospect references the report verbally and the contact has no tracked touch (e.g., security team forwarded PDF internally).

---

3) RULES OF THE ROAD (so reporting isn’t garbage)

- Do not create ad-hoc UTMs.
- Outbound sequences must use the canonical links (with UTMs) from the playbook.
- Webinar recording follow-up emails must use utm_source=webinar (not email) so we can isolate performance.
- Partners: use utm_source=partner + partner name in utm_content.

---

4) CADENCE

- Weekly (Mon 9am PT): pipeline + meetings + influenced rollup to GTM leads
- Biweekly (every other Wed): exec view (Camila/Jordan) with trendline + top segments
- 30-day post-launch: attribution audit (spot-check 20 deals) + adjust definitions if needed

If this looks good, reply “approved” or leave edits by EOD. I’ll update INT-9322 notes and push the final into the campaign folder.

Attachments:
- Benchmark_Launch_Attribution_Playbook_v1.0.pdf
- UTM_Naming_Conventions_Benchmark_Launch_v1.csv

—
Lauren Bishop
Marketing Ops / Attribution
Redwood Inference


---
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jul 22, 2025 at 10:02 AM PT
Subject: Re: Post-launch: pipeline attribution + tagging conventions (Benchmark Report)

This is solid.

Two questions:
1) For “influenced,” can we align on the window being 90 days? (Some of the enterprise cycles are longer; I don’t want Sales to argue it’s undercounting.)
2) Can we have a separate line for “benchmark referenced (self-reported)” vs “tracked touch”? I’m already seeing prospects forward screenshots internally.

Also: I’d like to be able to filter by segment (PLG vs enterprise) if possible.

-Ben


---
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jul 22, 2025 at 10:34 AM PT
Subject: Re: Post-launch: pipeline attribution + tagging conventions (Benchmark Report)

Re: 1) 90 days is my recommendation because it stays defensible and aligns with how we’ve done prior campaigns.

If we want to accommodate longer enterprise cycles, we can do:
- Primary influenced metric: 90 days
- Secondary “long-window influenced”: 180 days (reported as an appendix / dashboard toggle)

Re: 2) Yes — we can split influenced into:
- Influenced (tracked): contact has a HubSpot-recorded benchmark campaign touch
- Influenced (manual): deal has “Influenced campaigns (manual)” contains benchmark_report_2025

That should cover the forwarded-PDF scenario without us over-assigning credit.

Segment filtering: we can filter by Lead Source / Lifecycle stage at create + Sales pipeline (SMB vs ENT). I’ll add those filters to the dashboard view.

Can we add a short “How to tag outbound” section (2–3 bullets) that Markus/Stephanie/Lukas can drop into the enablement doc? We need to prevent AEs from pasting raw /benchmarks links without UTMs.

Also +1 to 90-day primary and 180-day secondary.

-Soojin

Subject: Re: Post-launch: pipeline attribution + tagging conventions (Benchmark Report)

+1, and a practical question:

If an AE is emailing a prospect a PDF directly (attachment) vs using the landing page, do we want them to:
- link to the landing page anyway (with UTMs), and/or
- add the manual influenced field when the prospect says they saw it?

We’re getting “saw your latency/$ chart on LinkedIn” replies where the click tracking won’t always show up.

-Steph

Date: Tue, Jul 22, 2025 at 3:38 PM PT
Subject: Re: Post-launch: pipeline attribution + tagging conventions (Benchmark Report)

All — incorporating feedback. Proposed final:

A) Outbound tagging (copy/paste for enablement)
- Always use the canonical benchmark link from the playbook (it includes UTMs). Do not paste “/benchmarks” raw.
- If sending the PDF as an attachment due to corporate restrictions, include the canonical link in the email body anyway.
- If the prospect explicitly references the report but there is no tracked touch, set deal field “Influenced campaigns (manual)” = benchmark_report_2025.

B) Influenced windows
- Primary: 90-day influenced
- Secondary: 180-day influenced (dashboard toggle; clearly labeled)

C) Dashboard filters
- Add: owner team (NA/EMEA) and deal pipeline segment (SMB/ENT where available)

I’ll push the updated playbook + UTM CSV to the campaign folder and update the HubSpot dashboard by tomorrow morning.

Camila — if you want the exec rollup to include influenced-by-region (EU vs US), I can add that as a second tab, but it may be noisy until we have ~2 weeks of volume.

—Lauren
